pharm: A long-acting PDE5 inhibitor that increases cyclic GMP to promote smooth-muscle relaxation; relaxes corpus cavernosum to enhance erection, relaxes prostate/bladder smooth muscle in BPH, and produces pulmonary vasodilation in pulmonary arterial hypertension.

summary: Tadalafil (CIALIS for erectile dysfunction and benign prostatic hyperplasia; ADCIRCA for pulmonary arterial hypertension) is a long-acting PDE5 inhibitor. By inhibiting PDE5 it raises cyclic GMP, causing smooth-muscle relaxation: in penile tissue this enhances nitric-oxide-mediated erection, in the prostate and bladder it relieves lower urinary tract symptoms, and in the pulmonary vasculature it lowers pulmonary artery pressure. Its long half-life (about 17.5 hours) allows once-daily or as-needed dosing with a wide window of effect. It is absolutely contraindicated with any form of organic nitrate or guanylate cyclase stimulators (e.g., riociguat) because of potentially fatal hypotension. Other key risks include hypotension with alpha-blockers and antihypertensives, non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) with sudden vision loss, sudden hearing loss, and prolonged erection/priapism. Exposure is increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors.
indications: Signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)
Erectile dysfunction and BPH occurring together
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to improve exercise ability (ADCIRCA)

dosage.n: Effect can persist up to 36 hours

admin: Take orally with or without food
For as-needed ED dosing, take before anticipated sexual activity; sexual stimulation is required for an erection
For once-daily ED/BPH dosing, take at about the same time each day regardless of activity timing
For PAH, take both 20 mg tablets together once daily; do not divide the dose across the day
Do not use with any nitrate medication or guanylate cyclase stimulators
moa: Tadalafil is a selective, reversible inhibitor of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-specific phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5). Sexual stimulation releases nitric oxide in the penis, which activates guanylate cyclase to increase cGMP, relaxing corpus cavernosum smooth muscle and allowing inflow of blood to produce an erection. By inhibiting PDE5, the enzyme responsible for cGMP degradation, tadalafil increases and prolongs cGMP levels, enhancing the erectile response; it has no effect without sexual stimulation. PDE5 is also present in prostatic, bladder, and urethral smooth muscle, where increased cGMP relieves BPH symptoms, and in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle, where it produces vasodilation and reduced pulmonary artery pressure in PAH.

absolute: Concurrent use of any organic nitrate (e.g., nitroglycerin, isosorbide), regularly or intermittently - risk of profound, potentially fatal hypotension
Concurrent use of guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat - symptomatic hypotension
Known serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, urticaria)
relative: Cardiovascular disease for whom sexual activity is inadvisable (recent MI/stroke, unstable angina, uncontrolled arrhythmia, severe heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension or hypotension)
Left ventricular outflow obstruction, severely impaired autonomic control of blood pressure
Hereditary degenerative retinal disorders (e.g., retinitis pigmentosa)
History of NAION or anatomic penile deformity/conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell, myeloma, leukemia)
monitor: Blood pressure, especially when combining with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives

preg: Tadalafil is not indicated for use in women. There are limited human data; available data have not established a drug-associated risk of major birth defects. Animal studies did not show adverse developmental effects at clinically relevant exposures. When tadalafil is considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension in a pregnant woman, the decision should weigh maternal benefit against potential risk.
lact: Tadalafil is not indicated for use in women. There are no data on the presence of tadalafil in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production.
renal: For erectile dysfunction as-needed dosing, the maximum dose in patients with creatinine clearance 30-50 mL/min is 5 mg not more than once daily, and with CrCl <30 mL/min or on hemodialysis the maximum is 5 mg not more than once every 72 hours. Once-daily ED and BPH dosing is not recommended in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min). For PAH, avoid use in severe renal impairment; if CrCl is 31-80 mL/min start at 20 mg once daily and increase to 40 mg as tolerated.
hepatic: In mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B), as-needed ED dosing should not exceed 10 mg once daily. Tadalafil has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); use is not recommended. Once-daily dosing for ED or BPH is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment. For PAH, use is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment because it has not been evaluated.

major: Organic nitrates (nitroglycerin, isosorbide mono-/dinitrate, amyl nitrite/poppers) - profound additive hypotension; contraindicated
Guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) - symptomatic hypotension; contraindicated
Alpha-blockers (doxazosin, tamsulosin, etc.) - additive blood-pressure lowering and symptomatic hypotension/syncope
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - markedly increase tadalafil exposure; limit dose
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce tadalafil exposure and efficacy
Other PDE5 inhibitors - do not use together (additive effects, no added benefit)
Bosentan - may reduce tadalafil exposure (relevant in PAH)
minor: Antacids may slightly slow tadalafil absorption (rate, not extent)
interactions.food: Tadalafil may be taken with or without food; the rate and extent of absorption are not affected by food.
interactions.alcohol: Both tadalafil and alcohol act as mild vasodilators; substantial alcohol intake (e.g., 5 or more units) combined with tadalafil can increase the potential for orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, and headache.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory diagnostic interactions; monitor blood pressure clinically when combining with antihypertensives or alpha-blockers.

serious: Symptomatic hypotension (especially with nitrates, alpha-blockers, or antihypertensives)
Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) with sudden vision loss
Sudden decrease or loss of hearing, sometimes with tinnitus and dizziness
Serious cardiovascular events in predisposed patients
rare: Hypersensitivity reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and exfoliative dermatitis
emergency: Erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism) - seek immediate care
Sudden vision loss in one or both eyes
Chest pain or symptoms of severe hypotension/syncope after dosing

monitoring: Blood pressure, particularly when starting alpha-blockers or antihypertensives
Erectile and lower urinary tract symptom response
Duration of erection and signs of priapism
counsel: Never use this medicine with any nitrate heart medication or 'poppers' - the combination can cause a dangerous, possibly fatal drop in blood pressure
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting longer than 4 hours, or for sudden loss of vision or hearing
For as-needed ED use, sexual stimulation is needed for it to work and the effect can last up to 36 hours
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially alpha-blockers, blood pressure drugs, antifungals, and HIV medicines
Limit alcohol, which can add to dizziness and low blood pressure
pk: ED effect generally within about 30-45 minutes (as-needed dosing)
Median time to peak plasma concentration about 2 hours (range 30 min-6 hr)
ED efficacy can persist up to 36 hours after a single as-needed dose
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Absolute contraindication with all nitrates and with riociguat - check before prescribing and warn about recreational nitrites (poppers)
Long half-life (~17.5 h) gives a ~36-hour window for as-needed ED dosing and supports once-daily use for ED and BPH
Initiate alpha-blockers and tadalafil cautiously and at the lowest dose to avoid symptomatic hypotension
Counsel on NAION (sudden vision loss) and sudden hearing loss - stop and seek care immediately
Reduce dose with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors and in renal/hepatic impairment; PAH uses the fixed 40 mg once-daily Adcirca dose
missed: For once-daily ED or BPH dosing, take the missed dose as soon as remembered the same day; if it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. For as-needed ED dosing there is no schedule to miss; take only before anticipated activity and no more than once daily. For PAH, take the missed dose as soon as remembered, but skip it if close to the next dose; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: In overdose, employ standard supportive measures as needed. Single doses up to 500 mg have been given to healthy subjects and multiple daily doses up to 100 mg to patients; adverse events were similar to those seen at lower doses but may occur more frequently. Hemodialysis contributes negligibly to tadalafil elimination because of its high protein binding. Manage hypotension and prolonged erection (priapism) according to standard care.
